title: Add Bold Tag in String
description: You are given a string `s` and an array of strings `words`. Every occurrence of any word inside `s` should be shown in bold. Mark each character of `s` that is covered by at least one occurrence of a word. Then wrap every maximal run of marked characters in a single `` and `` pair. Overlapping occurrences and occurrences that touch end-to-start must end up inside the **same** pair of tags. Return the resulting string. If nothing matches, return `s` unchanged. **Example 1:** ``` Input: s = "hello42world", words = ["hell","world"] Output: "hello42world" Explanation: "hell" covers indices 0-3 and "world" covers 7-11; the two runs are separated by "o42", so they get separate tags. ``` **Example 2:** ``` Input: s = "mmnnop", words = ["mm","mn","nop"] Output: "mmnnop" Explanation: "mm" covers 0-1 and "mn" covers 1-2, so they overlap; "nop" covers 3-5 and touches that run. Everything merges into one bold block. ``` **Example 3:** ``` Input: s = "abcdef", words = ["xy","fg"] Output: "abcdef" Explanation: Neither word appears in s, so no tags are added. ```

examples.explanation: "hell" covers indices 0-3 and "world" covers 7-11; the two runs are separated by "o42", so they get separate tags.
"mm" covers 0-1 and "mn" covers 1-2, so they overlap; "nop" covers 3-5 and touches that run. Everything merges into one bold block.
Neither word appears in s, so no tags are added.

constraints: s and words[i] consist of English letters and digits
All values in words are unique
solution_approach: Brute force: for every start index i and every word w, check whether s starts with w at i and mark those characters bold; this is O(n * m * L) time for n = len(s), m words of max length L. With a trie: insert all words, then from each index i walk the trie along s[i:] and remember the farthest end j of any word reached; mark s[i..j-1] as bold (or maintain a running 'bold until' pointer). Finally scan once, opening when entering a bold run and closing when leaving it, which merges overlapping and adjacent ranges automatically. The trie walk costs O(n * L) time and the trie uses O(total word length) space, plus O(n) for the bold mask.
hints: Instead of thinking about tags directly, first decide for each character of s whether it should be bold.
From each starting index you want the longest word that starts there. A trie of the words lets you find every match starting at i in a single walk.
Keep a boolean mask (or a running 'bold until' index). After filling it, build the output by inserting where a bold run begins and where it ends, so touching ranges merge naturally.
follow_up_questions: How would you support case-insensitive matching while keeping the original casing of s?
If s were extremely long and words fixed, how would Aho-Corasick improve the matching phase?
